THE RECEIPTS

Small numbers. Fully checked.

An original hand-worked example using the standard inertia-weight PSO equation. The app recomputes each value with the same engine used in the lab.

One particle. One update.

v′ = w v + c₁ r₁ (p − x) + c₂ r₂ (g − x)
x′ = x + v′

Minimize f(x, y) = x² + y². Start with x = (2, 1), v = (0.4, −0.2), personal best p = (1, 1), and global best g = (0, 0).

w = 0.5c₁ = 1c₂ = 2r₁ = (0.5, 0.5)r₂ = (0.25, 0.25)
CalculationBy handEngine resultCheck
The new position is (0.7, 0.4).

Its fitness is 0.7² + 0.4² = 0.65. This improves on personal best fitness 2, so personal memory becomes (0.7, 0.4). The existing global best at (0, 0), with fitness 0, stays unchanged.

Tolerance: 10⁻¹⁰. No speed or boundary limit is triggered in this example. Fixed random factors make every term independently checkable.

Follow the arithmetic

Momentum

0.5 × (0.4, −0.2)
= (0.2, −0.1)

Personal memory

1 × 0.5 × ((1, 1) − (2, 1))
= (−0.5, 0)

Swarm knowledge

2 × 0.25 × ((0, 0) − (2, 1))
= (−1, −0.5)

Add, then move

v′ = (−1.3, −0.6)
x′ = (2, 1) + (−1.3, −0.6)
= (0.7, 0.4)

This is our own arithmetic example, not a copied textbook result. The underlying algorithm follows the referenced PSO formulation.

Engelbrecht · Chapter 16 ↗
A FIELD GUIDE TO COLLECTIVE INTELLIGENCE

Each particle has a very simple job.

Search for a position with a smaller function value. Remember what worked. Share the best discovery.

◌

Explore a landscape

A particle is a candidate solution: a pair of coordinates (x, y). Height is the objective function’s value. The map shows that height as color: pale valleys are better, dark purple regions are worse.

Sphere has a minimum of 0 at (0, 0). Rastrigin has many local traps and a global minimum of 0 at (0, 0). Rosenbrock’s minimum is 0 at (1, 1).

✣

Three influences, one move

Inertia preserves direction. Personal pull returns to the particle’s own best discovery. Social pull heads toward the best point the entire swarm has found.

Independent random factors r₁ and r₂, sampled in [0, 1) for each coordinate, keep the motion varied. A seed makes the experiment repeatable.

⌁

Watch learning happen

We minimize all three functions. Only improvements replace personal and global memories, so the best-so-far curve cannot go up. A particle’s current fitness can still get worse.

A flat curve may mean convergence or stagnation in a local minimum. Reaching the iteration budget does not prove a global optimum was found.

Three experiments worth trying

  1. Remove the crowd: set social pull to 0. What information disappears?
  2. Add momentum: compare inertia 0.2 and 1.1 with seed 42. Do particles overshoot?
  3. Make the landscape harder: switch to Rastrigin and compare seeds 42 and 7.

What this implementation does

Uses synchronous, global-best PSO. All velocities use the same previous global best. Speed is limited per coordinate to 20% of the domain width. At a boundary, a coordinate is clamped and that velocity component becomes zero. Memories update only after the whole swarm is evaluated.

Initial velocities span ±5% of domain width. Stops at your iteration budget. No automatic optimum detection or convergence guarantee.

Algorithm reference: Engelbrecht, Computational Intelligence, Chapter 16. Learning inspiration: VisuAlgo. Interface, code, and worked example created for Swarm Lab.
